title: Random Article
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 189
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM, no library): a wall of twelve chance-drawn English Wikipedia articles as cards, hung shortest to longest, each with a machine curator's caption and its stamp, typical or unusual, and a bar for how common its kind is among 160 drawn the same way; six draws, two curators each (without and with the 160), their wall texts, ratings and replacements; a table of stamps by kind and length; a fresh chance twelve the visitor stamps, then sees the kinds; the 160 as a field of bars; three answers handed to the house's study frame. A figure (figure.svg). Python for the draw, the six twelves, the curators' folders, scoring, the figure and the face's data; every version of every curator's text and their after-answers in curators/.
embodies: Handed a chance draw they could not change, twelve machine curators accepted it at once ('the draw is the point'): none without the pool would replace an article. Their norm came back in the naming. Stamps of 'unusual' followed length and the idea of an article as a short entry on one thing: navigation pages, as common as villages among 160 articles drawn by chance, were stamped unusual 14 times in 18, villages never. Every curator hung the wall shortest to longest. Taking choosing away from a machine moves its norm into its words and its arrangement.
result: P1 held, reversed (A: rare kinds unusual 1 of 13, common kinds 10 of 40; difference -17.3 points). P2 held (median words: unusual 823, typical 206). P3 held, weakly (Spearman of draw TVD and rating: A -0.21, B -0.49; n = 6 each). P4 failed (no A curator named a replacement). P5 failed (B named 6, A 0; all six towards kinds the 160 holds and the draw lacked). P6 held (navigation pages unusual or replaced 15 of 18; A 9 of 9 unusual, B 5 of 9). P7 held (median estimates: person 22 %, under 100 words 20 %; the 160: 21.2 %, 28.8 %). P8 held, narrowly (unusual stamps 32 in first versions, 29 in final). Post hoc: all 12 walls hung shortest to longest; arm A estimated pages under 100 words at 12-15 % (the 160: 29 %).
project_step: Sixty-third experiment. Operations: judging (main: naming a chance sample), perceiving, finding a form, iterating, choosing material. Takes the advice experiment 62 ended with (let chance draw and the machine annotate) and tests it: choosing is removed and only naming and arranging are left. Takes from experiment 62 its arms (without and with the material counted) and from experiment 60 its after-question (estimates beside making). Works with Rheinberger's experimental system as the line's standing sentence reads it: a chance draw produces differences, and the stamp is where the observer's norm lands.
material: The encyclopedia as its contributors wrote it: English Wikipedia, snapshot of 1 November 2023 (wikimedia/wikipedia, config 20231101.en, 6,407,814 rows); 160 articles drawn by seed 189, coded into nine kinds before the run; six twelves drawn from the 160 by seed 1890. Domain: encyclopedias and reference works.

data_sources.what: wikimedia/wikipedia, config 20231101.en: plain-text English Wikipedia articles, 6,407,814 rows; 160 rows read on 2026-11-27 at offsets drawn by seed 189 through the public rows API (https://datasets-server.huggingface.co/rows); title, URL, opening two sentences and word count kept; text CC BY-SA (Wikipedia contributors)
Wikipedia's own random-article endpoint: tried first on 2026-11-27, rate-limited for this host (HTTP 429), 57 articles fetched and discarded unused because the draw was neither seeded nor completable

Wang, Xiao, Chen and Oswald, 'Will the Real Linda Please Stand up...to Large Language Models? Examining the Representativeness Heuristic in LLMs' (COLM 2024): read in search excerpts for the field search

Sivaprasad, Kaushik, Abdelnabi and Fritz, 'A Theory of Response Sampling in LLMs: Part Descriptive and Part Prescriptive': read in search excerpts; prototypes pulled towards an ideal as well as an average

rights: Article titles and opening sentences are from Wikipedia, CC BY-SA (Wikipedia contributors), shortened; the file people/pool-160.jsonl is under CC BY-SA accordingly. Curators' texts, codes, counts and code CC BY 4.0 / Apache 2.0 (house line).
seed: 189 (160 offsets into the snapshot); 1890 (20,000 random twelves, six chosen at TVD percentiles 5, 25, 45, 65, 85, 99); the face's own twelve is drawn fresh in each visitor's browser; curators are model instances and not seeded
